- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks, especially in early 30d window.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model underestimates downside risk; increase early forecast lows and adjust downward momentum in later days.
- Model often overshoots after sharp sentiment spikes (e.g., +0.67 → +1.00), leading to overreaction; cap forecast peaks at 1.5–2x recent high if sentiment shifts.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized; if 30d forecast shows persistent upward trend with low sentiment, reduce slope and add downward bias in middle-to-late window.
- Horizon-specific: 1–5 day forecasts are often too optimistic; 20–30 day forecasts show overconfidence in upward momentum; apply decay factor to later days if sentiment is weak.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “+0.33 → -0.33” transitions, model tends to misread trend reversal; adjust forecast mid-point downward by 10–20% in such cases.
